title: Who a ZDX probe runs for: probing and exclusion criteria

prose.text: A probe runs only for the users its criteria select, and the two criteria sets use opposite logic. {{inclusion-and}} {{exclusion-or}}

checks.do: Whether the exclusion criteria, evaluated first, remove the users the probe was meant for when a probe returns no data.
Whether every populated inclusion field matches the user, since inclusion fields combine with AND.

inclusion-and.statement: Probing (inclusion) criteria use AND logic across fields: a probe for user John Doe, user group Group B and department Finance has the expression John Doe AND Group B AND Finance.

quotes: When you want to include criteria for a probe, the probe uses the AND logic.
Expression: John Doe AND Group B AND Finance

exclusion-or.statement: Exclusion criteria use OR logic and stop probing data from being gathered for what they select: excluding user group Group C and department Finance gives NOT (Group C OR Finance).

quotes: When you want to exclude criteria for a probe, the probe uses the OR logic. The Exclusion Criteria avoids gathering probing data for the selected criteria.
Exclusion Criteria: - User Group: Group C - Department: Finance - Expression: NOT (Group C OR Finance)

multi-item-or.statement: Several items selected within one field combine with OR, in both probing and exclusion criteria: locations San Jose and Los Angeles with user groups Group B and Group C give (San Jose OR Los Angeles) AND (Group B OR Group C), and excluding locations Sacramento and San Francisco and departments Engineering and Finance gives NOT (Sacramento OR San Francisco) AND NOT (Engineering OR Finance).

quotes: You can select multiple items within the field criteria that uses the OR Logic. This is applicable to both the Probing and Exclusion Criteria.
Expression: (San Jose OR Los Angeles) AND (Group B OR Group C)
Expression: NOT (Sacramento OR San Francisco) AND NOT (Engineering OR Finance)

exclusion-first.statement: When probing and exclusion criteria are combined, the exclusion criteria are evaluated first and then the probing criteria: probing Group B in California while excluding Finance and San Jose gives NOT (Finance OR San Jose) AND (Group B AND California).

quotes: The Exclusion Criteria is evaluated first and then the Probing Criteria.
Expression: NOT (Finance OR San Jose) AND (Group B AND California)

worked-example.statement: Under that combined example, a Group B user in California in the Finance department is not probed, a Group B user in San Jose is not probed, and a Group B user elsewhere in California outside Finance is probed.
worked-example.conditions: Applies the help's expression NOT (Finance OR San Jose) AND (Group B AND California); assumes, as the example implies, that the California location contains San Jose. The help does not walk through individual users.

os-selection.statement: OS selection is supported for end user probe configurations.

quotes: The OS selection is supported for end user probe configurations.

using-criteria.statement: OR expands results, AND reduces them, and combining inclusion with exclusion criteria decreases probe results; if no results are found, Zscaler recommends reducing the amount of criteria.

quotes: Using OR can expand your results.
Combining inclusion and exclusion criteria decreases the amount of your probe results.
If you do not find any results, Zscaler recommends reducing the amount of criteria.

contract-criteria-fields.statement: In the API contract a monitor carries inclusion lists `onUsers`, `onGroups`, `onDepartments`, `onLocations`, `onLocationGroups`, `onGeolocations` and `onDevices`, and matching exclusion lists `excludedUsers`, `excludedGroups`, `excludedDepartments`, `excludedLocations`, `excludedLocationGroups`, `excludedGeolocations` and `excludedDevices`, each an array of at most 100 items.
